findings.description: The RDS instance sets storage_encrypted = false, so the underlying EBS volumes, automated snapshots and logs holding application data are stored in cleartext with no KMS key. Anyone obtaining snapshot access or underlying storage access reads the data directly.

publicly_accessible = true assigns the MySQL instance a public endpoint reachable from the internet, removing the VPC network boundary that should isolate the data tier. Exposure then depends entirely on the security group, leaving no defence in depth against a future rule change or misconfiguration.

The user_data script interpolates the RDS master password (var.password) and username into /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc. EC2 user-data is retrievable in cleartext from the instance metadata service by any local process or via SSRF in the hosted PHP app, and is also visible to anyone with ec2:DescribeInstanceAttribute.

The inline policy grants s3:*, ec2:*, and rds:* on Resource "*", giving the web server near-administrative control over all storage, compute and database resources in the account. Compromise of the internet-facing instance escalates immediately to account-wide data access and privilege escalation (e.g. ec2:RunInstances with PassRole-equivalent effects, rds:RestoreDBInstanceFromDBSnapshot).

No metadata_options block is specified, so the instance defaults to allowing IMDSv1 (http_tokens = "optional"). Combined with the wildcard IAM role and a public PHP application, a server-side request forgery flaw can trivially retrieve role credentials and the user-data containing the DB password.

The MySQL 8.0 parameter group does not set require_secure_transport = 1, and the generated PHP client uses mysqli_connect with no TLS options, so application-to-database traffic including the master credentials and employee records travels unencrypted.

The database security group permits all protocols to 0.0.0.0/0. A compromised database host has an unrestricted outbound channel for data exfiltration or command-and-control; a data-tier security group has no legitimate need for open internet egress.
The master username is hard-coded to "admin", a well-known default that removes one unknown from credential-guessing attacks against the publicly accessible endpoint.

The master password is supplied via var.password and is additionally interpolated into EC2 user-data, so it is persisted in cleartext in the Terraform state file and plan output rather than being sourced from Secrets Manager or generated with manage_master_user_password.

No root_block_device with encrypted = true is specified, so the instance volume holding dbinfo.inc with the plaintext database password may be written to unencrypted storage depending on account defaults.
